text.font-family: 'Playfair Display', Georgia, 'Times New Roman', 'Liberation Serif', serif

text.tspan: The Palma ratio is a measure of inequality that divides the share received by the richest 10% by the share of the
poorest 40%. Higher values indicate higher inequality. Depending on the country and year, the data relates to
income (measured after taxes and benefits) or to consumption, per capita. The chart shows breaks in the
comparability of the underlying household survey data over time within each country individually.

tspan.tspan: World Bank Poverty and Inequality Platform (2026)
